trickyParts: Relay and hub generations: start and stop under one mutex; a stopped generation publishes only into its own subscriber-less stream; Add on the WaitGroup only while not closed (event_stream_relay.go, delivery_live_hub.go).

The SSE live loop dedupes on one rising id; an overflowed subscription re-subscribes before cancelling the old one and catches up within the replay bounds, while a generation end (reset, test hook, shutdown) still ends the response so the browser reconnects.

Pending comment_deliveries rows are inserted in the comment's transaction with claimed_at null so a queued send left at SIGTERM is recoverable; the sender claims them with claimCommentDeliveryAttempt(initial=true).

A timed-out mention lookup carries no suppression, except that a route string equal to the timed-out mention's target suppresses the route copy (architect's decision); differing strings resolving to one session get two copies (tests pin both).

The delivery hub records what each event touched while a view's read is in flight and re-checks it against the installed answer, so an event during a read is not lost and an unrelated session write causes no second recompute.
The route lookup runs in a goroutine beside resolveMentionTargets; on a ROUTE_CHANGED retry the mentions are kept and only the new route is looked up (comment_create.go resolveCommentLookups).

Recovery waits only for live claims taken before the sender's first read (the database's now()), so a busy sender never reschedules for its own claims; a claim of a process killed after this one started is recovered by that process's own restart.
GET /api/v1/events/log pages the whole log by id for any authenticated caller, the same audience the SSE stream already serves.
deviations: The restart scenario (T1) is built on legion/INFRA-589 and attached as dispatch://INFRA-606/artifact/infra606-restart-scenario-patch; it lands in this PR in the next implementing round, after INFRA-589 merges (architect's decision A, Envoy 2026-10-27T14:03Z), with at least five runs per side per step.
The plan's expectation that Dispatch CPU in the minute after the restart falls below base was not observed beyond run-to-run noise at two runs per side; recorded as measured in the PR body.
Added beyond the plan: the spec's API-3 line (an overflowed SSE subscriber is caught up from the database instead of closed) and a hub race fix (an event during a view's read).
X-Dispatch-Event-Replay: complete is set by this PR server-side (INFRA-492's client reads it); INFRA-492's architect was told the rule over Envoy.
No partial index for the recovery pass's comment_deliveries query: it runs once per process start (and after a queue overflow drains); a new migration would collide with main's numbering.
New read route GET /api/v1/events/log (not in the plan): the only way the Stage 3 audit can read events that belong to no issue once the stream's replay is bounded.

Mention recovery is one periodic stranded pass per process (start + every 30 s) over attempts at least a claim lease old, replacing the start pass, the lapse timer and the drain-triggered pass; the lease-age rule keeps a pass from taking a live process's queue out of order, at the cost of up to a lease of extra latency for a stopped process's leftovers.
The Stage 3 audit falls back to the event-stream replay when production answers the log route 404 (warn-first), per the architect's ruling on review finding 3.

Reviewer's fast-follow done in this round (architect's ruling): hub generations own their views and conns (nine currency guards gone), deliveryHub.feed removed, the relay and the log route share readEventsAfterID, signal(q.wake), mention process tests moved to shutdown_mentions_test.go.

Two forward merges of main (both on GitHub-reported conflicts), each fingerprinted on the PR. The second takes main's outbox/publisher.go whole (#2225) and drops this branch's claim-token edit and payload reopen in favour of extending main's leftToMention.
A send that waits in its lane longer than model.DeliveryClaimLapse unclaimed is counted abandoned by main's outbox query, which then publishes the copy; the mention may also land (documented).

The outbox settles an abandoned mention attempt only for a session or target a held-back copy asks about, so a mention no copy covers is still left to the stranded pass; settling also appends the comment.delivery receipt through the broker.

The outbox counts an attempt a sender claimed as abandoned only past model.StrandedMentionWindow (one hour, moved from the API to model so both read one value); within it a lapsed claim leaves the copy to the stranded pass without deferring. A resend that then fails for good leaves the session with whatever the first send delivered.

The outbox's claim guard in recordBatch is back (a batch never marks published a row reopened after it read it), as agreed in writing with INFRA-590's implementer, because a failed mention now reopens comment.created.
The fallback copy carries the failed mention's dedupe key; a same-mode retry after the copy reached the session is then recorded duplicate and dropped (named in the PR body's risk line).
